reading.body:
CyrusOne Quincy is the largest disclosed data center in Washington by IT capacity, at 36 MW, but that figure covers only two of 46 mapped facilities in the state.

The campus spans 720,000 square feet of technical space, giving it about 50 watts per square foot, a density consistent with high-performance compute rather than general-purpose colocation. At a typical AI training density of 40 kW per rack, 36 MW would support roughly 900 racks, though the operator publishes no tenant mix or workload type, so that is an upper bound on AI-specific capacity, not a confirmed deployment.

For AI scaling, the binding question is power. CyrusOne publishes no certifications and no utility partnership details for this campus, so its grid connection, available headroom, and ability to expand beyond 36 MW are unknown. Washington has 46 mapped data center facilities, but only two disclose capacity, meaning the state's true compute footprint is largely invisible and this campus's 60 percent share of declared load may overstate its regional importance.
